functional: Approving accepts both UNDER_DIRECTOR_REVIEW and UNDER_BUDGET_OFFICER_REVIEW. This is the documented two-scenario rule: budget-then-director, or director alone.
Rejecting accepts only UNDER_DIRECTOR_REVIEW, so a request cannot be rejected at a stage it has not reached.
Approving requires a signature; the URL is copied onto the request so a later profile change cannot alter the record.
Rejecting does not require a signature.
Approving sets three columns at once — directorReviewStatus, idoFinalStatus and masterStatus — plus the signature pair, all in one transaction with the audit log.
masterStatus becomes UNDER_IDO_FINAL_REVIEW, which is the first time since submission that the requestor's view moves.
The approval trail states whether the budget officer has signed, so approving ahead of them is a visible choice.
Once approved, this page opens read-only; the Director's next involvement is the final approval page (spec 014), which the staff dashboard routes to.
authorization: Server gate: roleProcedure('DIRECTOR') on both, then assertPermission(APPROVE_DIRECTOR), then the stage check, then — for approval — the signature check.
The stage check reads directorReviewStatus, never masterStatus, which cannot distinguish the budget sub-stage from the director sub-stage.
A BUDGET_OFFICER or IDO role calling either procedure gets FORBIDDEN.
The same DIRECTOR role also owns the final approval (spec 014); the two are separated by the column they read, not by the role.
ux: The approval is a confirmation dialog naming what it does — stamps a signature and sends the request to the IDO Chairperson.
When the budget officer has not signed, the dialog says so plainly rather than leaving the Director to notice an absence.
Reject is hidden, not disabled, while the budget stage is open — a disabled control invites a search for the missing precondition, and here there is nothing the Director can do to enable it.
A missing signature is explained on the page with a link to the profile before an attempt is made.
Both controls are disabled while either mutation is in flight.

edge_cases: The asymmetry between approve (two states) and reject (one state) is deliberate and is the single most fragile rule in the workflow. Any refactor that unifies the two guards breaks the documented behaviour.

A director approving while the budget officer is mid-approval is a genuine race: whichever transaction commits first wins, and the loser's guard then refuses. Both outcomes are correct; the UI must show the refusal as 'already moved on', not as an error.
The signature URL is copied, not joined — an already-stamped approval must not change when the director updates their profile picture of a signature.
Approving writes five columns; all of them plus the audit log belong in one transaction, or a partial failure leaves a signed request that never moved.

The Director appears twice in the workflow with the same role. resolveReviewRoute (spec 009) keys on finalDirectorStatus to tell the two apart, and this page must open read-only for a request that has reached the final stage rather than trying to act on it.
masterStatus moves here for the first time since submission; the requestor's counters and list must be invalidated even though nothing about the requestor changed.
out_of_scope: The Director's FINAL approval — spec 014, a different page with a different guard.
The IDO Chairperson's final review — spec 013.
Delegation or an acting director — there is one DIRECTOR role and no delegation model.
